Acceptance ① (all production launch sites owned or non-executing): the measured inventory is encoded in a CI guard whose 17 allowlist entries each carry a reason and an owner — guardian/supervisor/helper family, the P23 supervised transport, the Codex-account exception, the pinned bwrap verification, five gateway legacy sites owned by P28/P29, two documented test-only seams — and any fresh Command::new / LocalShellBackend::new outside that list fails CI; the guard caught two seam sites on its own first run that the grep inventory had missed, which is the guard doing its job. Acceptance ② (local backend test-only): the last production LocalShellBackend consumer (TUI bang) is migrated to an honest Unsupported, the production composition's FakeProcessService is replaced by the real dormant ManagedProcessService (no binding, read-only floor, refuses before anything exists), and zero production callers remain for both local-shell constructors. Acceptance ③ (no capability activation): nothing activated — the startup gate call regenerates the boot's report row and prints the honest Unsupported verdict, s24a pins that an Activated verdict cannot appear, and the s04 wiring pins hold untouched. App-side impact stated plainly: plugins' host.process.* now reaches the real supervised surface, which refuses with the dormant-floor reason instead of fake-succeeding, and TUI `!` commands print an honest unavailable notice instead of running unsandboxed — both are the contract's requirement and INV-07's, and both are disclosed here rather than buried.
